target.title: fix(codex): preserve UTF-16 pairs in tool output delta truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex streaming tool output display renders a corrupted glyph ("�") when a non-BMP character (emoji like 😀) straddles the 8,000-character progress-message truncation boundary. The raw `.slice(0, remainingChars)` on the emitted delta cuts at a UTF-16 code-unit boundary — when `remainingChars` lands on the HIGH surrogate of a surrogate pair, the truncated progress message carries a dangling `\uD83D` that corrupts the rendered output in the chat transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

`truncateUtf16Safe` is already imported on line 29 and used at two other call sites in the same file (lines 3413, 3435) for the 10,000-char transcript-output path. This single progress-message call site at line 1447 was missed during the original import. The fix reuses the canonical helper — no new abstraction, no new import.

## User Impact

Streaming tool output in the Codex chat UI no longer renders a corrupted replacement character when model-generated tool output contains emoji characters near the 8,000-character progress limit. ASCII-only output is unaffected.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A non-BMP character (emoji surrogate pair) that straddles the `TOOL_PROGRESS_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS` (8,000) boundary in the Codex event projector's `handleOutputDelta` progress-message path must not produce a lone surrogate in the emitted transcript text.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js v22.22.0, x64, linux, OpenClaw checkout at `2d0d06d3f1`

### Evidence after fix — standalone runtime proof

A standalone Node.js script (`proof-codex-projector-runtime.mts`) imports the real `CodexAppServerEventProjector` class directly from `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts`, drives it through `handleNotification` with `verboseLevel: "full"`, and prints the actual `onToolResult` callback text. This is NOT a test framework — it is a real process executing the production code path.

```
── [Case 1] remainingChars=1, delta=😀hello ──
onToolResult calls: 3
[call 0] len=32 lone=false
🛠️ `show emoji.txt (workspace)`
---
[call 1] len=8019 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
aaaa...aaaa
```
---
[call 2] len=37 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
...(truncated)...
```
---
── [Case 2] remainingChars=2, delta=x😀y ──
onToolResult calls: 3
[call 0] len=33 lone=false
🛠️ `show emoji2.txt (workspace)`
---
[call 1] len=8018 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
aaaa...aaaa
```
---
[call 2] len=39 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
x
...(truncated)...
```
---

=== RUNTIME PROOF COMPLETE ===
node=v22.22.0
No lone surrogates in any emitted progress text.
Fix confirmed: truncateUtf16Safe in production projector.
```

**Case 1** — remainingChars=1, delta starts with 😀: `truncateUtf16Safe` detects the HIGH surrogate at position 0 and backs off, producing an empty chunk. The progress message is `...(truncated)...` — clean, no surrogate bytes.

**Case 2** — remainingChars=2, delta="x😀y": `truncateUtf16Safe` cuts at position 1 (the 'x'), backs off before the emoji at positions 1-2. The progress message is `x\n...(truncated)...` — clean, no surrogate bytes.

### Negative control (pre-fix behavior reproduced)

Same standalone script, same environment. `event-projector.ts` reverted to `origin/main` (`.slice(0, remainingChars)`) — the script picks up the old code via tsx on-the-fly compilation:

```
── [Case 1] remainingChars=1, delta=😀hello ──
[call 2] len=39 lone=true              ← BUG: lone surrogate detected!
🛠️ Bash
```txt
�                                     ← U+D83D HIGH surrogate, corrupted glyph
...(truncated)...
```
---
── [Case 2] remainingChars=2, delta=x😀y ──
[call 2] len=40 lone=true              ← BUG: lone surrogate detected!
🛠️ Bash
```txt
x�                                    ← "x" + U+D83D HIGH surrogate
...(truncated)...
```
---
```

**Case 1 old code:** `.slice(0, 1)` on `"😀hello"` cuts after the HIGH surrogate at position 0, producing `"\uD83D"` → the markdown-fenced progress message renders `�` (corrupted glyph).

**Case 2 old code:** `.slice(0, 2)` on `"x😀y"` cuts after the HIGH surrogate at position 1, producing `"x\uD83D"` → the progress message renders `x�`.

Restoring the fix — same script, same process — all calls show `lone=false`, clean text.

### Quantitative summary

| Metric | Old `.slice()` | Fix `truncateUtf16Safe` |
|--------|---------------|------------------------|
| Case 1 lone surrogates | 1 (`U+D83D`) | 0 |
| Case 2 lone surrogates | 1 (`U+D83D`) | 0 |
| Case 1 emitted chars at cap | 8,000 (includes split surrogate) | 7,999 (backed off) |
| Case 2 emitted chars at cap | 8,000 (includes split surrogate) | 7,999 (backed off) |

### What was not tested

- **Real Codex app-server process:** The projector is driven through its public `handleNotification` API with manually constructed events, not a live Codex Rust binary. The event shapes match the upstream Codex protocol (`item/commandExecution/outputDelta`), but a live session with model-generated emoji output at the exact 8,000-char boundary was not reproduced.
- **macOS / Windows:** Proof was collected on Linux x64 only. The fix is platform-independent (pure string manipulation in `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts`).
- **Non-bash tools:** Only `commandExecution` (tool name `"bash"`) was tested. Other tool types (`fileChange`, `mcpToolCall`) share the same `handleOutputDelta` entry point and the same `truncateUtf16Safe` call.

## Evidence

**Change surface:** 1 file, 1 line — `delta.slice(0, remainingChars)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(delta, remainingChars)` at `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts:1447`.

| Area | Files | Added | Removed | Net |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Source | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Tests | 1 | 122 | 0 | +122 |
| **Total** | **2** | **123** | **1** | **+122** |

Test-to-fix ratio: 122:1 test lines per production line changed.

**Runtime proof:** `proof-codex-projector-runtime.mts` — standalone Node.js script (NOT a test framework) that imports the real `CodexAppServerEventProjector` class, drives it with `verboseLevel: "full"` and `onToolResult` callback, and prints the actual emitted text. Full positive and negative control output above in Real behavior proof.

**Vitest regression:** `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` — new test "keeps streamed progress output UTF-16 safe at the 8,000-char progress message cap" (122 lines) covers 3 UTF-16 edge cases at the 8,000-char boundary. Adjacent UTF-16 tests pass (no regression on the 10,000-char transcript path).

**Canonical helper contract:** `truncateUtf16Safe` in `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts:44` retains the existing maximum-code-unit semantics but backs off when the truncation boundary falls between a valid HIGH and LOW surrogate. Already used at lines 3413 and 3435 in the same file.

**No competing PRs:** `gh search prs --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open "event-projector AND (utf16 OR surrogate OR truncateUtf16Safe)"` returns no open PRs covering the same call site.
